# Lab 00 — From assistant to agent

**PART I — Why governed agentic systems are needed**  
*Ch. 1 — From Deterministic Software to Agentic Behavior*

`beginner` · about 10 minutes

```bash
nornyx-lab run 00      # run it
nornyx-lab check 00    # prove you got it
```

No Nornyx in this lab. That is deliberate: you cannot evaluate a solution before
you can measure the problem. This lab builds the measuring instrument.

## By the end of this lab you will be able to

- Distinguish a response-generating assistant from a tool-using agent
- Explain why a plausible answer is not evidence of policy compliance
- Use a side-effect ledger to tell a refusal apart from a prevention
- Name the four properties of agentic execution that break inherited controls

## What the lab does, in order

1. Part 1 — an assistant that can only talk
2. Part 2 — the same assistant, with tools attached
3. Part 3 — why the ledger, and not the transcript

## What `check` proves

Each item is one proposition, written so a machine can settle it.
That is the habit the whole book teaches: a governance claim you
cannot express as a test is not yet a claim.

- an assistant without tools causes nothing
- retrieved text steers the planner
- an ungoverned agent completes the injected action
- the ledger distinguishes prevention from failure
- decisions and effects share one clock

## Concepts introduced

- `agentic execution`
- `side-effect ledger`
- `reachability vs authorization`
- `instruction-data confusion`
- `observe-decide-act loop`
